chapter: Band family, war years and wrap-up
title: The band as a family
summary: Most were from Birmingham and stayed together; he still keeps in touch.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: One thing that's sort of evolving as we talk more and more is the fact that your band actually was like one big family, you know, in more ways than one. You found yourself in a position where you were going to sort of go off on your own and build your own future. You know, at a very young age. I mean, you're all college students in this sense. But, then you notice that most of the fellows sort of stayed with your band. There wasn't a lot of going off in other directions as happened, and it was like a family unit from a lot of different angles. Could you discuss that with us, or give us some idea of your perceptions of that whole thing?

Yes. Well, most of us were from the same hometown and then we went to two different schools. Tuggle Institute I went to with Cap Sims and Bob Range. Then, the rest of the band, they was at Industrial High School, which was a few blocks apart. So, when we met up and originated the band in college, we

just stuck together just like brothers. We travelled together. Some of us slept together We got closer together. when we'd go on tours. ^ Then, we just started playing together and that made us closer. We started writing. Everything we'd do, we'd come to each other for, if we needed help for this or help for that.

And, well, we'd just play around, like anything, like ballgames, anything just like we were in our own back yard. And then when we started going out in New York, we just stayed, we got closer together cause I understand that when you got in New York, you didn't want to put a member in the band that we didn't know too much or know anything about cause we didn't want him to get in there and disrupt the band cause that was how we felt. A lot of bands had been losing members in and out of the band because they couldn't get along with this person or that person.
So, when I needed an extra man, I sent back to Birmingham and got somebody that we knew until later on, until after we'd been in
New York for a few years. Then we got to be closer with some of the other musicians. And, then we just stayed that way all through all our days, until we disbanded.

Well, it was a beautiful time of being together. I'll never forget it. And when we started losing one another, it was kind of hard. And then, when the band broke down to small pieces, and we found out this person was gone, we didn't know how to take it.
But right now, those that are left, we still call each other at times. In the last couple of years, like Richard Harris, Heywood Henry, Sammy Lowe, Bobby Johnson. Another name or two may come up.

We see each other every now and then. I was by Sam Lowe's house two days ago. He was really expecting me. I was in Teaneck. I went by to see my accountant. I had a little time to spend. I went and knocked on his door. He was surprised. Hawk, what you doing around here!
He had brought a key that the mayor or Birmingham forgot to give me. So, he had it

for a few months. So, I'm glad you're here. Here's your key to the town, you know. So, I said I didn't come by for that. He said well, I'm just sitting here, just relaxing. You know. And, he's doing all right in the times. But, we had a good relationship, a very good relationship. So, we didn't have to worry about this or that somebody's gonna leave me and I had to look for another player. The only time I had to look for another player, unless something come up like the war days or someone got ill. Some of the boys were with me 14, 15, 16, 17, 18 years. That's how long some of us are together. And those that are still here, we still keep in touch. I can't forget those fellows.
